title: Extend QCLI-270's flag-naming fix to the 15 positive-gate action dispatchers (migration backlog, milestone, decision, draft)
description:
Follow-up filed per QCLI-270's own instruction to record scope discovered outside its acceptance criteria as a new task rather than a silent addition. QCLI-270 (Done) fixed 21 of 37 call sites of the shared only(parsed, allowed) usage-error idiom in src/cli/main.ts to name the actual rejected flag (via the new unknownFlags()/usageFailure() helpers) instead of a generic, sometimes-misleading fallback sentence.

The remaining 15 call sites -- the migration-backlog (preview/apply/status/rollback), milestone/decision (list/view/create/delete/edit/archive), and draft (list/view/create/promote/archive) action dispatchers -- use a different shape: a *positive* if (action === x && only(parsed, allowed)) { ...; return ...; } gate per action, cascading on failure to ONE shared bottom-of-group fallback message (e.g. "milestone action is invalid or missing required arguments"). By the time that fallback runs, which action's allowlist actually failed is no longer known, so usageFailure cannot be dropped in without restructuring the whole if/else-if cascade per group. QCLI-270 judged this a materially larger, riskier change than its own two named commands warranted and left it as a documented structural gap (see src/cli/main.ts's comment above usageFailure, ~line 375, and QCLI-270's own implementation notes) -- this task is that restructure.

Known, accepted risk: a caller of any of these 15 dispatch actions with a valid reference/actor but one extra unrecognized flag currently gets the generic per-group fallback message instead of the specific flag name -- the same class of misdiagnosis QCLI-270 fixed everywhere else in the CLI.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each of the 15 identified call sites (migration backlog preview/apply/status/rollback; milestone list/view/create/delete/edit/archive; decision list/view/create/delete/edit; draft list/view/create/promote/archive) reports the specific unrecognized flag via usageFailure or an equivalent, not the shared per-group fallback, when the actual failure is an unrecognized flag

Every other rejection reason within these same action dispatchers (missing reference, unparseable arguments, an invalid action name) still gets its original, correct message -- QCLI-270 explicit requirement carried forward
bun run check exits 0, including new test coverage exercising the flag-naming path for at least one action per group (migration backlog, milestone, decision, draft)
src/cli/main.ts's comment documenting this as a known structural gap (~line 375-382) is updated or removed once the restructure lands, so the code no longer describes a gap that has been closed

plan: Restructure the 4 migration-backlog action gates (preview/apply/status/rollback) so an unrecognized flag is named via usageFailure while a missing reference keeps the group fallback
Restructure the 6 milestone/decision positive gates (list/view/create/delete/edit/archive) the same way
Restructure the 5 draft positive gates (list/view/create/promote/archive) the same way
Update the structural-gap comment in the usageFailure docblock so it no longer describes a closed gap
Add test coverage naming an unrecognized flag for one action per group, then run bun run check
